articles.text:
2. Where are you going?

In Lesson 1, you learned that 'How are you?' functions in English primarily as a greeting and that the expression is not usually used to make an inquiry about the listener's health. The comparable Japanese expression, Ogenki desu ka?, is used both as a greeting and as an inquiry about health.

In this lesson, you will learn another such formula. When you go out, your neighbor may say something like the following:

(Ima) odekake desu ka?         Are you going out (now)?
Dokoka e odekake desu ka?      Are you going somewhere?

If a person is not familiar with the way these expressions are used, it might seem that the Japanese are very nosy. However, these are routine expressions used as part of a greeting and should not be taken literally. Just like English 'How are you?', they are used to acknowledge a human relationship. Since this is the case, you don't really have to give exact answers to the 'inquiry.' A typical answer is Ee, chotto (soko made) 'Yes, just over there.'

Similarly, when you come home, your neighbor may say:

(Ima) okaeri desu ka?    Are (you) coming home (now)?

You can simply answer Ee to this greeting.
